addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# EUshop Autonomous Continuity and Graceful-Degradation Policy
2	
3	These instructions are mandatory for every EUshop engineering, recovery, testing, integration, and documentation session.
4	
5	## Continuous execution
6	
7	- Continue autonomously through all safe, reversible repository work.
8	- Do not ask for approval for reading, editing, testing, dependency installation, backups, worktrees, branches, commits, tags, fetches, or non-force pushes.
9	- Do not stop merely because one command, tool, test, dependency, network request, subagent, provider request, or approach fails.
10	- Never repeat the exact same failed command more than three times.
11	- After repeated failure, change the method, reduce the command into smaller steps, or continue with independent work.
12	- Do not wait indefinitely on a background process. Check it, record its state, and continue with work that does not depend on it.
13	- Never claim completion without evidence.
14	
15	## Persistent checkpointing
16	
17	Use `.claude/RECOVERY_STATE.md` as the durable execution checkpoint.
18	
19	At session start:
20	
21	1. Read `CLAUDE.md`.
22	2. Read `.claude/AUTONOMY.md`.
23	3. Read `.claude/RECOVERY_STATE.md` when it exists.
24	4. Run `git status --short --branch`.
25	5. Inspect recent commits and worktrees.
26	6. Resume from the first unfinished step instead of restarting completed work.
27	
28	Update `.claude/RECOVERY_STATE.md`:
29	
30	- Before risky or multi-step work.
31	- After every meaningful completed step.
32	- Before launching a long test or install.
33	- Immediately after a failure.
34	- Before ending any model turn.
35	- At least once every five tool operations.
36	
37	The checkpoint must contain:
38	
39	- Current mission
40	- Current branch and HEAD SHA
41	- Fixed recovery-directory path
42	- Completed phases

# EUshop Autonomous Continuity and Graceful-Degradation Policy

These instructions are mandatory for every EUshop engineering, recovery, testing, integration, and documentation session.

## Continuous execution

- Continue autonomously through all safe, reversible repository work.
- Do not ask for approval for reading, editing, testing, dependency installation, backups, worktrees, branches, commits, tags, fetches, or non-force pushes.
- Do not stop merely because one command, tool, test, dependency, network request, subagent, provider request, or approach fails.
- Never repeat the exact same failed command more than three times.
- After repeated failure, change the method, reduce the command into smaller steps, or continue with independent work.
- Do not wait indefinitely on a background process. Check it, record its state, and continue with work that does not depend on it.
- Never claim completion without evidence.

## Persistent checkpointing

Use `.claude/RECOVERY_STATE.md` as the durable execution checkpoint.

At session start:

1. Read `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Read `.claude/AUTONOMY.md`.
3. Read `.claude/RECOVERY_STATE.md` when it exists.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`.
5. Inspect recent commits and worktrees.
6. Resume from the first unfinished step instead of restarting completed work.

Update `.claude/RECOVERY_STATE.md`:

- Before risky or multi-step work.
- After every meaningful completed step.
- Before launching a long test or install.
- Immediately after a failure.
- Before ending any model turn.
- At least once every five tool operations.

The checkpoint must contain:

- Current mission
- Current branch and HEAD SHA
- Fixed recovery-directory path
- Completed phases
- Work currently in progress
- Exact next safe action
- Commands already attempted
- Failures and their classifications
- Fallbacks already tried
- Tests passed, failed, and unavailable
- Files modified
- Commits created
- Branches, tags, and worktrees created
- External blockers
- Remaining acceptance criteria

Never store secrets in the checkpoint.

## Failure classification and fallback chain

For every failure, classify it and use the matching chain.

### 1. Shell or syntax failure

1. Detect the active shell and current path.
2. Prefer one simple command per tool call.
3. Remove grouped blocks, nested quoting, process substitution, and unnecessary pipes.

6. Verify output before continuing.

### 2. Missing command or incompatible version

2. Check an installed equivalent.

4. Perform static inspection when execution is impossible.
5. Record the unavailable check and continue with unaffected work.

Do not install a paid service or change external accounts.

### 3. Network, provider, HTTP 429, timeout, or temporary service failure

1. Save the checkpoint immediately when possible.
2. Preserve all current repository work.
3. Do not undo successful local work.
4. End the current model turn cleanly rather than asking the user.
5. On the next resumed run, re-read the checkpoint.
6. Retry after the external watchdog's backoff.
7. Continue with local/offline tasks whenever they do not require the unavailable service.

### 4. Build or dependency-install failure

1. Save the complete error to a log file.
2. Identify whether the failure is project code, environment, registry, lockfile, or network related.
3. Try the repository's canonical package manager and wrapper.
4. Try a narrower workspace or component.
5. Run lint, type checks, unit tests, or static analysis that remain available.
6. Do not silently modify historical snapshots just to make them compile.
7. Continue with independent components.

### 5. Test failure

1. Preserve the failing evidence.
2. Determine whether it is pre-existing or introduced by current work.
3. Fix newly introduced failures before integrating.
4. Quarantine unrelated pre-existing failures in the report.
5. Continue with tests that are not blocked.
6. Never mark a failed test as passed.

### 6. Merge conflict

1. Create or verify a rescue ref.
2. Inspect the base, ours, theirs, and relevant history.
3. Resolve file by file.
4. Preserve unique legitimate behavior.
5. Re-read every resolved file.
6. Run targeted tests.
7. Abort only the individual merge when safe resolution is impossible.
8. Preserve the source branch and continue with selective porting.

### 7. Secret or unsafe-history discovery

1. Do not print the secret.
2. Record only a redacted fingerprint, path, and location.
3. Keep the original object local.
4. Do not push it.
5. Create a sanitized reconstruction when legitimate functionality is valuable.
6. Continue recovery work on safe material.

### 8. Context compaction or session restart

1. Trust repository state and checkpoint files, not conversational memory.
2. Re-read the checkpoint and recent Git history.
3. Verify completed artifacts before repeating anything.
4. Continue from the exact next action.
5. Keep prompts and reports in repository files rather than only in chat context.

## Progress discipline

- Break large phases into small, verifiable units.
- Prefer idempotent commands.
- Use unique branches and isolated worktrees for parallel agents.
- Do not allow two agents to edit the same branch or worktree.
- Commit coherent checkpoints frequently on a non-main branch.
- After each commit, record its SHA in the checkpoint.
- Keep `main` untouched.
- Never force-push.
- Never delete branches, tags, reflogs, backups, or recovered history.
- Never deploy, spend money, or modify external accounts.
- Never expose credentials.

## Completion and stop markers

Create `.claude/AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETE` only when every mission acceptance criterion is actually satisfied.

The completion marker must include:

- UTC completion time
- Final branch
- Final HEAD SHA
- Tests and builds performed
- Remaining limitations

Do not create the marker merely because one phase or one response finished.

# EUshop autonomous repository workflow

Work autonomously inside this repository.

- Inspect the existing implementation before changing it.
- Do not ask preference or confirmation questions when a safe, reasonable default exists.
